mission_header.title: Mission status
mission_header.what_for: Where the mission is and how cut off from Earth you are. Messages to the ground take minutes each way and may not get through during a blackout, so the crew acts first.
mission_header.how_to_read: Day {day} of {duration}. Comms delay is the one-way time for a message to reach Earth.
mission_header.blackout_active: Communication blackout: messages to the ground are held until the link returns. Use the onboard crew medical officer for anything that cannot wait.
mission_header.blackout_inactive: No blackout simulated for this day.

radiation_budget.title: Radiation budget
radiation_budget.what_for: How much space radiation you have received this mission, and where you are heading by mission end, compared with NASA's 600 mSv career limit.
radiation_budget.how_to_read: Solid bar: dose received so far. Lighter bar: projected total if the background rate continues ({rate} mSv/day). Prior missions are included only if known.
radiation_budget.career_unknown: Your dose from earlier missions is not recorded here, so the career total is unknown. Only this mission is shown.
radiation_budget.source_note: Limit: NASA-STD-3001 Vol 1 Rev C. Background rate: measured on the way to Mars (Zeitlin et al. 2013).

today_tiles.title: Today
today_tiles.what_for: One tile per health area. Each compares today's readings with your own normal, measured in the 14 days before launch.
today_tiles.how_to_read: Nominal: within your usual range. Watch: a sustained change worth checking. Act: follow the card now. No reliable data: readings are missing or too few to judge — this is not the same as normal.

attention_cards.title: Needs attention
attention_cards.what_for: The next steps for anything flagged. Urgent items always appear first and are never hidden; routine items are limited to three so the list stays readable.
attention_cards.how_to_read: Each card says why it appeared, how sure the system is, what to do now, when to check again, and who to involve. Urgent cards are marked Act.
attention_cards.empty: Nothing needs attention today. Keep wearing your sensors and completing check-ins so this stays reliable.

detail.title: Detail
detail.what_for: The evidence behind a tile: your recent readings against your preflight normal, what changed, and the suggested next step.
detail.how_to_read: The shaded band is your usual range. Gaps in a line are missing readings, not zeros.
detail.chart_legend: Line: your nightly reading. Dark line: your preflight normal. Shaded band: your usual range around it. Gap: no reading that night.
detail.no_action: No action is needed for this area today. The chart is shown for information.

crew_grid.title: Crew overview
crew_grid.what_for: Every crewmember's status in each health area on the selected day, so the crew medical officer can see who may need a check-in.
crew_grid.how_to_read: Select a cell to open that person's detail. In a real mission each astronaut would choose what is shared.

timeline.title: Mission log
timeline.what_for: Everything that happened, in order: when flags started and cleared, space-weather warnings, and actions recorded on this device.
timeline.how_to_read: Recorded actions show that a step was logged, not that it caused any later change.
timeline.empty: No changes recorded for this selection yet.

replay.title: Mission replay
replay.what_for: Play the simulated mission day by day to see when changes happen and when SpaceHealth flags them.
replay.how_to_read: Markers show when each simulated event really started. They are visible only here, never on the Today screen.

validation.title: Validation (simulated)
validation.what_for: How the detectors performed on simulated missions where we know the truth: whether each event was caught, how early or late, and how many false alerts occurred.
validation.how_to_read: These are synthetic-scenario results, not clinical validation.
validation.mock_note: These numbers are placeholder mock values for building the screen. They are not results from the SpaceHealth model.
validation.holdout_title: Frozen-model holdout test (run once, simulated missions)
holdout_lines: Illness-like change: flagged by the symptom day in 25 of 40 independent simulated cases (62 %), and within the illness period in 39 of 40. Larger heart-rate rises were caught earlier; the smallest (about 3–4.5 bpm) were usually caught 1–4 days after symptoms began.
Sleep restriction: flagged by day 97 in 26 of 40 cases; 11 were never flagged, mostly where the restriction was small compared with that person's normal sleep.
Solar particle events: every warning in the replayed NASA DONKI sequence raised an immediate Act for every crewmember.
Exercise-like heart-rate spikes: never escalated to Act. Missing data: always shown as No reliable data.
Routine false alerts: about 0.85 physiological and 0.44 sleep Watch episodes per 100 crew-days (roughly 1.5 and 0.8 per crewmember over a 180-day mission).
validation.holdout_note: The detector was chosen and its settings locked before this test. Results are synthetic-scenario results from our simulator, not clinical validation.
validation.release_case_note: The mission shown in this app is one pre-selected holdout case (seed 1000), chosen before results were seen.
validation.illustrative_case_note: Illustrative case: this simulated mission (holdout seed 1002) was chosen after testing to show every part of the interface. It is a typical success, not the best result. Overall results, including misses, are in Validation.
validation.preselected_case_note: Pre-selected case (holdout seed 1000), fixed before testing. Here the illness-like change is flagged one day after symptoms began and the sleep restriction is not flagged — see Validation.

theme.trajectory_note: Illustrative progress along a simulated transit; not a navigation display.
theme.comms_link: Message to Earth: about {minutes} min one way (illustrative)
theme.comms_blackout: Link down — messages to Earth are held until it returns
theme.storm_banner_body: Follow the mission's approved solar particle event procedure. Details are in the radiation card.
theme.storm_banner_note: Event timing replays real solar activity recorded by NASA's DONKI database (September 2017, observed near Earth).
theme.crew_badge_note: Simulated crewmembers C1–C4. Not real people.

states.load_error: SpaceHealth could not load or check its data files, so no health status is shown. Showing partial data could be misleading.
states.indicator_unavailable: No assessment is available for this area on this day. This is not the same as normal.

actions.recorded: Action recorded on this device at {time}. Recording a step does not confirm it was completed or that it changed anything.

glossary.baseline: Your personal normal, from preflight measurements.
glossary.unknown: Not enough reliable data to judge.
glossary.mSv: Millisievert, a unit of radiation dose.
glossary.CMO: Crew medical officer — the crewmember trained to provide medical care on board.
